riskTone.label: BULLISH
riskTone.rationale: Cool US inflation, solid bank earnings, and eased tariff threats on China/India all signal risk-on momentum supportive of UK100.

briefing.briefing: Starting with the currency picture: GBP/USD is up a small +0.1% today, sitting at a high 89th percentile of its last 20 days — and because UK100 and sterling move in opposite directions (a stronger pound makes the index's huge dollar-earning companies like Shell, BP, Unilever and AstraZeneca worth less in pound terms), this acts as a mild headwind for the FTSE, though the model flags the net effect as NEUTRAL at current levels. The broader regime is genuinely mixed: on the bullish side, US stocks closed higher overnight (S&P +0.18%, Nasdaq +0.67%) after cooler-than-expected US inflation data [meaning prices rose less than feared, encouraging investors to take on more risk] and solid US bank earnings — Wall Street's VIX fear gauge [a measure of expected market turbulence] is at 17.37, a completely normal reading with no stress signal. Energy is a positive, with Brent crude up +0.64%, which directly supports Shell and BP — two of the five biggest index weights. Miners are flat (copper barely moved, -0.05%), banks are neutral (10-year gilt yields eased 2 basis points [a tiny move]), and long-end gilt stress is absent, removing one key bearish risk. On the cautionary side, the overnight COT [Commitment of Traders — a report showing how large money managers are positioned] data shows currency speculators are heavily "crowded short" [piled into bets that sterling falls] on GBP, which is a contrarian signal pointing toward a potential GBP squeeze upward — that would be a further FTSE headwind. European peers are split (EuroStoxx50 +0.29% but DAX -0.58%), giving no clear directional lead. Recent catalysts: US Russia sanctions easing tariff pressure on China and India (reported ~10 hours ago) is positive for global risk appetite, and yesterday's cool US inflation + bank earnings (22 hours ago) drove Wall Street's overnight gains — these are the clearest explanations for the generally firm overnight tone. Directional bias is a cautious NEUTRAL leaning very slightly bullish (bias score +1): the global risk backdrop is supportive but sterling strength, split European markets, and crowded GBP short positioning cap the upside. Confidence is 4/10 — a major wildcard sits right here tomorrow morning: UK Monthly GDP for May prints at 07:00 BST tomorrow (1 July 16), a HIGH-impact release that could shift the sterling and gilt picture sharply before the open. Today's ORB context shows the market gapped down -27.5 points at the open (-0.26%) and has already broken the ORB [the price range formed in the first 15 minutes of trading: high 10471.3, low 10449] to the downside — with 45% of the 14-day average daily range [the typical daily price swing of ~130.9 points, so about 59 points] already consumed, there is still meaningful room to travel (~72 points of average range remaining), but the break is already in play. For the ORB trader, today looks more like a moderate-conviction short-bias trend day following the downside break, but the split European tape and neutral macro picture mean fakeout risk [a false break that quickly reverses] is elevated — watch for any reclaim of the ORB high at 10471 as a sign the break is failing. No scheduled UK data releases today, but tomorrow's 07:00 BST UK GDP print is a significant build-up caution — size positions conservatively this afternoon and into tomorrow's pre-market. Key levels to respect: overnight high 10490.6 (resistance), ORB high 10471.3 (the line in the sand for bulls today), current price ~10450.75, ORB low 10449 (the broken level, now potential support-turned-resistance), overnight low 10431.2 (next downside target), and prior day low 10411.7 as the bigger bearish extension target. The short is in play below 10449 but treat any push back above 10471 as a signal to stand aside — tomorrow's GDP number is the real event.
